name: Endeavour Bridge
facts: Opened in May 1951, the Endeavour Bridge began as two separate two‑lane spans, each carrying General Holmes Drive over the Cooks River toward Botany Bay's mouth.
In 1963, the bridges were widened by extending their decks between them, creating a single six‑lane structure that matched the simultaneous expansion of General Holmes Drive.
Named after HMS Endeavour, the ship that brought James Cook to Botany Bay in 1770, the bridge honors the explorer who first charted Australia’s eastern coast.
